title: Personal Training Packages: how an active corporate wellness enrollment uplifts the effective refund percentage
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Personal Training Packages product line and states how holding an active corporate wellness enrollment uplifts the percentage applied to a package's unused-session value at refund.

## Rule
The effective refund percentage starts from the tier's own base refund percentage. Where the member holds an active corporate wellness enrollment, that enrollment's own employer discount percentage uplifts the effective refund percentage as a loyalty concession, with only half of that percentage's weight added to the uplift; where no active corporate wellness enrollment is held, no uplift applies and the effective percentage is simply the tier's own base refund percentage. In no case may the effective percentage exceed 100; where the uplifted total would exceed 100, it is capped at 100.

## Points of judgement
- What is held: an active corporate wellness enrollment.
- What value it contributes: that enrollment's own employer discount percentage.
- What effect it has: only half of that percentage is added on top of the tier's own base refund percentage, and the result never exceeds 100 percent.
As a hypothetical illustration only (not any tier's actual listed rate), suppose a tier's base refund percentage were 77 and the linked active corporate wellness enrollment's own employer discount percentage were 30: half of that percentage -- 15 -- would be added, giving an effective refund percentage of 92. Suppose instead the tier's base refund percentage were already 93 and the contributed uplift would otherwise bring the total past 100: the effective percentage is capped at 100 rather than allowed to exceed it. Where the member holds no active corporate wellness enrollment, the effective percentage is simply the tier's own base refund percentage with no uplift.
